clue.text: Beg out loud for victim

indicators.note: something said out loud is heard rather than read, so the sound counts, not the spelling

parts.note: to pray someone is to beg or implore them

explanation.surface: Someone pleads loudly on behalf of a victim.
explanation.walkthrough: PRAY (beg, as in 'I pray you') and PREY sound identical.
explanation.definitionFit: Prey is a hunted creature, and by extension anyone who falls victim to a predator or swindler.

clue.text: Political leader retaining muscle in place of policy programme?

indicators.note: to retain is to keep hold of, so the outer piece keeps the others inside it

parts.note: PM is the Prime Minister, the political leader
lat is short for latissimus dorsi, a back muscle
'for' can mean instead of, as in 'swap this for that'

explanation.surface: A party leader is building muscle instead of making policy.
explanation.walkthrough: The muscle and 'in place of' are joined and then held inside the two letters for the Prime Minister. The question mark flags that a platform is only loosely a programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A party platform is its declared set of policies put before voters at an election.

clue.text: Yes, doper misused medicine

indicators.note: something misused is put to the wrong use, so these letters are wrongly arranged and must be set right

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drug cheat admits to misusing a medication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doper' and 'medicine' make the surface feel like a sports doping story, but the letters of the first two words are simply rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyedrops are a liquid remedy applied directly into the eye, a common kind of medication.

clue.text: Rat runs originally only open to some ordinary people

parts.note: to rat on someone is to grass, British slang for informing to the police
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: what comes originally comes at the very start, so each word contributes just its opening letter

parts.note: the first letters of these four words

explanation.surface: Rodent paths that are open to only some people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rat runs' reads as a phrase (back-street shortcuts), but the rat is a verb meaning to inform and the runs are a cricket letter. To grass is British slang for snitching.
explanation.definitionFit: The grass roots of a party or movement are its rank-and-file members, as opposed to the leadership.

clue.text: One level holds lift

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: rase is a variant spelling of raze, to level a building to the ground
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A single floor of a building contains a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Level' and 'lift' together suggest floors and elevators, but 'level' is the verb raze, here in its older spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something is to elevate it, and a raise is also a pay rise, so lift fits as verb or noun.

clue.text: Perhaps George Harrison's alternative version of Something's lacking energy

indicators.note: an alternative version is a reworking, so the remaining letters are rearranged
lacking means the letter for energy is left out of the title

parts.note: the song title Something with its 's, taken letter for letter
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: George Harrison's song Something reworked without its oomph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking energy' takes E out of SOMETHINGS to leave SOMTHINGS, and 'alternative version of' rearranges those nine letters. Harrison wrote the Beatles song Something.
explanation.definitionFit: A songsmith is a songwriter, and George Harrison is one example, hence 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: Figure holding more change in US dollars

indicators.note: to change something is to alter it, so these letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sum of money held in US dollars, more of it changing hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' looks like a sum of money, which suits the dollars, but it is a figurine. 'Holding more change' reads as one phrase; the split falls after 'more'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian doll is a hollow wooden figurine that opens to reveal a smaller one nested inside, and so on.

clue.text: Drug subject barely swallowed

indicators.note: barely suggests stripped bare, so the word loses its outer letters

parts.note: a topic is a subject of discussion
ate means swallowed food

explanation.surface: A drug that a patient only just managed to get down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barely' strips the T and C from TOPIC, leaving OPI.
explanation.definitionFit: An opiate is a narcotic derived from opium, such as morphine.

clue.text: Shakin' Stevens primarily pens terrible tracks

indicators.note: to pen an animal is to shut it in an enclosure, so one piece is enclosed
primarily means in the first place, so only the leading letters are used

parts.note: the first letters of both words of the singer's name
poor means bad or terrible in quality

explanation.surface: The rock and roll singer Shakin' Stevens writes awful songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pens' and 'tracks' suggest songwriting and recordings; here pens is an enclosure verb and tracks are footprints. Shakin' Stevens is a Welsh pop singer of the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoor is the trail of footprints or scent left by an animal, so spoors are tracks a hunter follows.

clue.text: I'm here, and I see myself returning

parts.note: 'Ah' is what you say on understanding, like 'I see'

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so this piece is written backwards

parts.note: me refers to oneself

explanation.surface: Someone announces their arrival and catches sight of their own reflection coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a spoken phrase standing for a spoken noise: the polite cough used to say 'notice me'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahem is the throat-clearing sound made to draw attention to one's presence, so it effectively says 'pay attention, I am here'.

clue.text: Very soft rejection of work over failure within ChatGPT?

indicators.note: a rejected thing is sent back, so everything is read in the opposite direction
one thing over another covers it like a lid, so a piece goes around the rest

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
a miss is a failure to hit
within means in
ChatGPT is a well-known example of AI, artificial intelligence

explanation.surface: A gentle turning-down of a piece of work because ChatGPT got it wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The opus abbreviation wraps a three-part phrase, 'miss in AI', and then the whole string is read backwards. The question mark marks ChatGPT as one example of AI.
explanation.definitionFit: Pianissimo is the musical direction, marked pp, telling players to perform extremely quietly.

clue.text: Far from the last answer, concealing a French bomb

indicators.note: concealing means hiding inside, so one piece is tucked within the other

parts.note: the previous entry is a direction to play very quietly, and its opposite is the direction to play loudly
un is the French masculine word for 'a'

explanation.surface: Nothing like the previous solution, hiding a French explosive device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The last answer' is 10-across, PIANISSIMO, and forte (loud) is musically far from it. 'Cost a bomb' is British slang for costing a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a bomb is a huge sum of money, exactly as a fortune is, as in 'it cost a bomb'.

clue.text: With faithful partner shuffling, Uno deck could save love

indicators.note: shuffling a card deck mixes it up, so the letters are rearranged
save means except, so the letter for love is left out

parts.note: the three words taken letter for letter
love is zero in tennis scoring, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A card player shuffling an Uno pack and rescuing a romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'save love' removes one O from UNODECKCOULD to leave UNDECKCOULD, and 'shuffling' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cuckolded is to have an unfaithful wife; someone not deceived that way has a faithful partner.

clue.text: Quick drink not initially accepted by Riddler

indicators.note: what is accepted is taken in, so this letter goes inside the other piece

parts.note: a riddle is a coarse sieve, so a riddler is something that sifts

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: The Riddler, the Batman villain, turns down a quick drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The Riddler suggests Batman's puzzle-setting foe, but a riddle is also a garden sieve. 'Not initially' looks like a negation and is just one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A snifter is British slang for a small, quickly taken alcoholic drink, as well as the glass for brandy.

clue.text: Rogue criticises celebrity's drunk state

indicators.note: what has been drunk has been taken in, so one piece is swallowed by the others

parts.note: to rap someone is to rebuke them
a lion is a celebrated person, as in 'literary lion'
Cal is an abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: A villain attacks a famous person for being intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' looks like part of the gossip, but it means 'taken in': the state slips between the two other pieces, which run together around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapscallion is a mischievous rascal or scoundrel, which is what a rogue is.

clue.text: Grub alone unusual here?

indicators.note: something unusual departs from the normal form, so these letters take an unexpected order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A place where ordering only food would be odd.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a lounge bar is mostly for drinking, so turning up just for grub (food) would be unusual there.
explanation.definitionFit: A lounge bar is the more comfortable room of a British pub, where people mainly go to drink.

clue.text: Get the attention of restaurant staff, refusing current refreshment choice

parts.note: a tap on the shoulder gets someone's attention

indicators.note: to refuse something is to turn it away, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a waiter is a member of restaurant staff
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Summon the waiter and turn down the latest drinks on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like 'present' or a currant; it is the electrical symbol, taken out of the server.
explanation.definitionFit: Tap water is a free option when ordering something to drink in a restaurant, as opposed to bottled.

clue.text: 6 maybe certain suspicious wife's left

parts.note: bound means certain, as in 'bound to happen'

indicators.note: what has left has gone away, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: wary means suspicious or cautious
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: Someone is sure that the wary spouse has walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' looks like a cross-reference to 6-down; it is the number. In cricket a ball hit over the rope without bouncing scores six, called a boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a six is one kind of boundary, a hit reaching the edge of the field; 'maybe' allows for the four as well.

clue.text: Express turned on to long-term viewer

parts.note: to couch an idea is to express it in particular words

indicators.note: something turned faces the other way, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: atop means on top of
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fast train is switched on for someone watching over a long stretch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express turned on' sounds like an excited reaction or a train; express is a verb here, and only 'on' is turned around.
explanation.definitionFit: A couch potato is a lazy person who spends hours on the sofa watching television, so a long-term viewer.

clue.text: Scottish team game

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Heart of Midlothian, an Edinburgh football club
second meaning: a trick-taking card game where players avoid one suit

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a single team playing a match. Heart of Midlothian is a Scottish football club known everywhere by the short name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edinburgh football club is universally called by this nickname, and the same word names a well-known card game.

clue.text: Worst part about providing packaging for Queen or Queen II?

indicators.note: packaging wraps around its contents, so one piece encloses the other
about can mean turned round, as in 'about face', so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the lees are the dregs at the bottom of a wine bottle, the worst part
QU is an abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: Criticism of the worst element of how the band Queen's album was packaged.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen II was the second album by the rock band Queen, following their debut 'Queen', so it is literally a follow-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A sequel is a follow-up work continuing an earlier one, as the second album was to the first.

clue.text: Majority of old genre to be revised soon

indicators.note: revising reworks material into a new form, so the letters are rearranged
the majority is most but not all, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Most of an outdated literary type will shortly be reworked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soon' sits at the end like part of the sentence, but it is the definition of an archaic word.
explanation.definitionFit: Erelong is an old-fashioned adverb meaning before long, so shortly or soon.

clue.text: Smooth victory for former leader

parts.note: a bald head or tyre is smooth
a win is a victory

explanation.surface: An easy election win for a politician who once led the country.
explanation.walkthrough: Stanley Baldwin was a British Conservative Prime Minister three times between the wars.
explanation.definitionFit: Stanley Baldwin led the UK government in the 1920s and 1930s, so he is a former national leader.

clue.text: Majority of smutty books having no point

indicators.note: the majority is most but not all, so the word gives up its final letter

parts.note: blue means risqué or smutty, as in blue jokes
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Most dirty books are pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having no point' looks like a verdict on the smutty books, but it is the definition, meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A blunt knife or pencil has lost its sharp tip, so it literally lacks a point.

clue.text: Meandering article sealed between two bits of boxing

indicators.note: a thing sealed between others is shut in the gap they leave, so it sits in the middle of them

parts.note: a round is one period of a boxing match
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A rambling piece of writing locked away between two parts of a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sealed between' places the article in the middle; the two bits of boxing are different words, one period of a fight and a whole contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A roundabout route or explanation wanders indirectly rather than going straight, which is what meandering means.

clue.text: Peak energy lost around Vietnam

indicators.note: lost around means the letters for energy go missing from around the rest of the country's name

parts.note: vim means vigour or energy

explanation.surface: A soldier's energy fading in the jungle of Vietnam.
explanation.walkthrough: V, I and M sit around the middle of VIETNAM; take them out and four letters remain.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is a volcanic mountain in Sicily, so a peak.

clue.text: Unity and equality at first replaced by very top

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word for equality, which is swapped for other letters

parts.note: parity means equality
so means very, as in so good
a lid is a top for a container

explanation.surface: A slogan joining unity and equality, with a call to the very top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first replaced by' swaps the opening P of PARITY for SO and LID.
explanation.definitionFit: Solidarity is the unity of a group bound by shared interests or aims.

clue.text: A track keeping M People together

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold on to it, so one piece holds the letter inside

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway, a track
taken as written

explanation.surface: A song that keeps the 1990s dance band M People together.
explanation.walkthrough: M People were a British dance-pop band, so 'M People' reads as one name; the M is a separate letter and 'People together' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An army is a large organised body of people, and loosely any great crowd gathered together.
